successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Bone, which 'lost its independence to the Dutch' after the 1905 South Sulawesi expeditions and came under direct administration

ledger.x: c. 1350: Bone begins with Manurung ri Matajang. Rulers' table 'Manurung ri Matajang (Mata Silompoe), 1350-1366'; infobox '14th century'; the body says the origins 'can be traced back to the early 15th century'.
1611: Bone submits and accepts Islam; Tenripalle To'Akkeppeyang reigns 1611-1626 (rulers' table).
1645: the rising ends in Gowa's favour.
1660: a Bugis revolt under Arung Palakka.
1660: the revolt 'was crushed' and Palakka fled; the page gives no month, and the contest is closed the same year.
1669: Bone, with the VOC, becomes the leading state of South Sulawesi.
1814: Bone's overlordship over South Sulawesi ends ('From 1669 until 1814').
1905: the Dutch South Sulawesi expeditions reach Bone, after wars in 1824 and 1859.
1905: Bone passes under direct Dutch administration (restored as a Dutch-sanctioned sultanate in 1931, joined Indonesia in May 1950).

wars.name: Bone's risings against Gowa
wars.outcome: The 1644 rising and the 1660 Bugis revolt under Arung Palakka were crushed; Palakka fled South Sulawesi.

wars.name: Makassar War
wars.outcome: Bone's Bugis under Arung Palakka fought with the VOC; the Treaty of Bungaya (18 November 1667) and the fall of Somba Opu in June 1669 made Bone 'the supreme principality in South Sulawesi'.

wars.name: Dutch wars against Bone
wars.outcome: Bone fought the Dutch in 1824, 1859 and 1905; the 1905 expeditions ended its independence.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes Bone's boundary; the page gives the capital, the area ('about 2,600 km2') and the neighbours (Wajo, Soppeng allies, Luwu a rival over the Cenrana River mouth) but no line.
